🌐🔥🇲🇽 While the Giants Fight, Mexico Multiplies: Its Share of US Imports Jumps to 16.9%

On June 22, Beijing blacklisted 10 US defense-linked firms and barred 46 more from government procurement — retaliation for the Pentagon adding 65 entities to its 1260H list. US–China trade has fallen to its lowest level since the 2009 crash. The world's two largest economies are decoupling in real time, and the supply chains are rerouting.

The data shows who gains. Mexico's share of US imports climbed from 13.8% to 16.9% in just the first two months of 2026. Washington demands Mexico slam the door on China — yet Mexico already set permanent 10–35% steel tariffs and duties on roughly 1,400 products on its own schedule, to protect domestic industry and jobs, not to obey an order.

Here's the hypocrisy: the US weaponizes "free trade" against everyone while lecturing Mexico about Chinese imports. Mexico's answer is sovereignty, not obedience — keep options open with every partner, take the nearshoring windfall, and refuse to become anyone's collateral. In a multipolar world, the country that multiplies its options is the one that wins.

🇲🇽🌐 Mexico Doesn't Wait: Sheinbaum Will Propose a 16-Year T-MEC Extension on Its Own Terms

On July 1, Mexico won't sit and wait for Washington's verdict. President Claudia Sheinbaum will sign a letter formally proposing a 16-year extension of the USMCA/T-MEC at the trilateral meeting. Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard was blunt: "July 1 marks the start of the review process, not the end of it." Mexico moved early — not because it's cornered, but to define the terms and kill the uncertainty Trump's tariff threats manufacture.

The math favors Mexico's calm. If any party refuses to extend, the treaty doesn't collapse — it automatically stays in force for 10 more years, and no one has filed the required six-month withdrawal notice. Despite Trump's 25% tariff theatrics, most US–Mexico trade still crosses the border tariff-free. The "worst case," Ebrard noted, is a decade of guaranteed access.

This is sovereignty as strategy: define your position before the other side defines it for you. Mexico negotiates from a $1.6-trillion trade bloc it helps anchor — while diversifying toward Europe, Asia and Latin America. Stability isn't granted from the north. Mexico is writing it down and proposing it first.

🇲🇽🛢️ 32,000 megawatts in five years — the biggest power build-out in Mexico’s history. "For the first time in history we have projects for 32,000 megawatts — that’s historic — in 6 years, 5 years." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the Expansion Plan 739 billion pesos, 70% renewable, public sector majority. National generation rises from 354 to 410 million MWh by 2030 — with the State supplying 61%.

🚨🇲🇽 US agents entered Mexico without complying with the National Security Law. "What we have flagged — and the Attorney General is investigating — is the entry of US agents without complying with the National Security Law, carrying out operations that should be exclusively Mexican." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on US operations in Mexico Asked about a report alleging Chihuahua’s governor collaborated with the CIA, Sheinbaum said the government has no such information — but restated its standing objection. Security operations on Mexican soil belong to Mexican authorities alone.

🇲🇽✊ 82,000 homes — and 80% of beneficiaries are women. "This is housing from the National Housing Commission, for everyone who isn’t an Infonavit beneficiary." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Miércoles de Vivienda, Michoacán The target was raised to 82,000 units — a 95% increase. The homes go to families the old system left out. In the showcased 448-unit complex, 80% of the families are women.

🇲🇽🌎 Mexico and Brazil trading technology, not selling out to foreign oil majors. "We’re very interested in the technology they’ve developed, and they’re interested in how we’ve improved fertilizer production." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on a joint Pemex–Petrobras proposal Sheinbaum floated Pemex and Petrobras jointly exploring the Gulf of Mexico. Petrobras cut deepwater exploration from ~10 years to as little as months; Mexico shares its fertilizer advances. South–South cooperation.

🇲🇽🏭 Mexico is building the largest solar plant in the Americas. "We’ll reach 1,000 MW of total capacity — the largest photovoltaic plant in the Americas. Total investment exceeds 1.4 billion dollars." — Emilia Calleja, CFE Director General Puerto Peñasco, Sonora — public and CFE-owned, not a private concession. The same plan includes the Oasis project in Baja California Sur: solar + batteries + green hydrogen.

🇲🇽🏭 By 2030 the State will supply 61% of Mexico’s electricity. "By 2030, the public sector will inject 61% of the nation’s electricity." — Luz Elena González, Secretary of Energy A reversal of the neoliberal model that handed generation to private firms. With the Expansion Plan, CFE and the State recover the majority of national power generation.
